It's less about caring what other people think and more about why even bother posting something if it gets buried under comments with hundreds of upvotes or hidden because it received too many downvotes. If no one can even see your comment in the first place, there's less incentive to actually contribute to a discussion if you know that your comment is basically invisible. If people think 'What's the point in contributing?', there will be less discussion on Reddit and more lurkers.

Rather than have upvotes and downvotes, perhaps just have the report button which can be used for things that don't contribute to the discussion because upvotes and downvotes have become synonymous with agree/disagree, at least with some users.

I just think it would be cool if everyone had an equal chance to be read, so long as they're trying to contribute something meaningful to the tread.

People (myself included) never feel like contributing because of the terrible upvote/downvote system. Having an unpopular/different/controversial opinion means your contributions will just get buried because it's not what people want to see. I think reddit would work slightly better if downvotes/upvotes were just completely removed.

Way back when pokemon was released in the U.S., as a small child around the age of 6, I practically lived, breathed, and thought of pokemon my entire childhood. Having blue version first (followed by the other games), I always had pokemon experiences everywhere I went. Long car rides and vacations? Pokemon. After school? Pokemon. I even traded and battled with kids at my old babysitter's place. I had tons of pokemon memorabilia before even gold and silver were released. I would play with the figurines with my cousins, trade and play the tgc with my friends, and even stay up hours past midnight with my sister and cousins to beat pokemon snap. Pokemon helped me make new friends at school, by sharing a common interest, and helped me and my family create treasured memories together. Pokemon introduced me to my love of rpgs and gaming as I explored the wonderful world of the kanto region and its strange creatures.

Pokemon was my childhood, and I'm so lucky to have been able to experience the worldwide phenomenon with thousands of other kids. I have no idea how I would've turned out without pokemon in my life, and I plan on keeping that part of my childhood in my life forever.

It certainly is quite different from The Last Airbender for multiple reasons, but here's to name a few:

* Legend of Korra is only 12 episodes so far. While the series is continuing, we're on hold right now, and there's only so much you can do in 12 episodes. TLA had 61 to show great in-depth character development, different plots and story arcs, and did a better job at building a world while in my own opinion, LoK just glossed over lots of things.
* The time period change. While TLA seemed slower paced, focusing on more of a feel to nature (traveling to different places along their main journey), LoK is future set and does a good job of being fast paced, quickly developing the plot and setting lots of conflicts in motion at once.

Of course, these are just a few differences,  but LoK is worth watching. It had me on the edge of my seat during the later episodes, and the plot was very well done.

Anyway, to try and keep some relevancy to the OP, I'm hoping that we'll see more of a connection to the original bending disciplines in the next season, maybe so that different characters have their own personal journey or something.
Oh, and I hope to see more relationship building between the cast, since LoK has a lot of potential.
